question: Which cranial fossa is the deepest and houses the cerebellum and brainstem?

options.A: Superior cranial fossa
options.B: Posterior cranial fossa
options.C: Middle cranial fossa
options.D: Anterior cranial fossa

explanation: The posterior cranial fossa sits at the base and back of the skull, cradling the cerebellum and brainstem. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T7#BMP111_U2_T7_h5)

question: A midwife collaborates with an agriculture extension worker to teach mothers about growing nutrient-rich crops. What concept does this illustrate?

options.A: Tertiary hospital referral
options.B: Intersectoral collaboration
options.C: Cold chain maintenance
options.D: Passive health surveillance

explanation: Working across different sectors like health and agriculture addresses the broader social determinants of health and nutrition. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T2#BMP117_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically included in the comprehensive scope of family planning services?

options.A: Offering pre-conception health screening for couples
options.B: Performing major orthopedic surgeries for injured patients
options.C: Providing youth-friendly adolescent reproductive education
options.D: Screening and treating sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Orthopedic surgery belongs to general trauma and surgery departments, not reproductive health and family planning. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T1#BMP224_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why does a normal pregnancy make a woman more prone to rapid clotting issues?

options.A: The body naturally increases clotting factors to protect against bleeding
options.B: The liver stops producing proteins during active labor
options.C: Blood volume decreases significantly during the third trimester
options.D: Platelet counts drop to zero right before delivery

explanation: Pregnancy is a high-clotting state by design, meaning the blood clots more easily to safeguard against blood loss during birth. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is strict privacy so important when offering sexual health care to teenagers?

options.A: It guarantees that laboratory results are always negative
options.B: It replaces the need for any diagnostic testing procedures
options.C: It prevents the spread of airborne respiratory illnesses
options.D: It encourages young people to seek timely medical care

explanation: Adolescents fear social stigma and parental reprisal; knowing their information is private makes them much more willing to visit clinics. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is a stress test ordered when a patient's resting ECG is completely normal?

options.A: Resting ECG machines are unable to detect electrical signals from the left ventricle.
options.B: Ischemia may only appear on electrical tracings when the heart is working under increased demand.
options.C: It proves that the patient has never experienced any form of plaque buildup.
options.D: It permanently clears any existing blockages from the coronary blood vessels.

explanation: Mild or moderate artery narrowing may not show signs on an ECG until exercise increases the heart's need for oxygen. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T3#BMP125_U2_T3_h5)

question: When is the comprehensive postnatal check traditionally scheduled for mother and baby?

options.A: At one year postpartum
options.B: At six weeks postpartum
options.C: At twenty-four hours postpartum
options.D: At six months postpartum

explanation: The six-week visit is the milestone check where the midwife assesses complete physical recovery and reviews family planning. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant woman who walks barefoot on damp soil in a farming community presents with severe anaemia. Which parasite is the likely cause?

options.A: Necator americanus
options.B: Trichuris trichiura
options.C: Ascaris lumbricoides
options.D: Enterobius vermicularis

explanation: Necator americanus is a type of hookworm. Its larvae live in warm, damp soil and infect humans by burrowing through the skin when walking barefoot. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T7#BMP116_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why are cholinergic drugs strictly contraindicated in clients with a physical intestinal blockage?

options.A: The patient will experience severe hair loss and skin rashes
options.B: The medication will instantly dissolve and cause systemic poisoning
options.C: Increased muscle contractions can cause the blocked organ to rupture
options.D: Blocked intestines completely destroy the active molecules of the drug

explanation: Forcing a blocked bowel or bladder to contract harder with a cholinergic drug creates dangerous pressure that can lead to perforation. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T4#BMP124_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which procedure is used during antenatal care to check the baby's position and lie?

options.A: Postnatal lochia assessment
options.B: Leopold's maneuvers
options.C: Partograph plotting
options.D: Active management of the third stage

explanation: Abdominal palpation using Leopold's maneuvers is the standard clinical method to determine fetal position and presentation during antenatal visits. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the benefit of including experienced mothers in peer counseling sessions?

options.A: They take over the clinical examinations from the midwife
options.B: They handle the documentation of all medical records
options.C: They provide financial loans to pregnant women in need
options.D: They share relatable stories that help reduce cultural fears

explanation: Peers offer trusted, lived experiences that resonate deeply with pregnant women and encourage healthy practices. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T1#BMP227_U1_T1_h6)

question: At what stages of a health project should community involvement happen?

options.A: Strictly during the final evaluation report writing
options.B: Only after the government finishes building the clinic
options.C: Only when emergency funds run out unexpectedly
options.D: During both planning and implementation phases

explanation: True participation means community members are involved right from the initial planning stages through to executing the health activities. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is considered the gold standard imaging tool for diagnosing and evaluating an ovarian cyst?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Abdominal X-ray
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Pelvic ultrasound provides clear visualization of the ovaries, allowing clinicians to assess the size and internal structure of the cyst. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T7#BMP310_U3_T7_h4)

question: During which stage of pregnancy does the absolute daily demand for iron increase the most?

options.A: Immediately during active labor
options.B: The first four weeks after conception
options.C: Second and third trimesters
options.D: First trimester only

explanation: As blood volume expands rapidly and the fetus grows quickly in late pregnancy, iron needs peak significantly during the second and third trimesters. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T9#BMP118_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which medication is the first choice for treating eclamptic fits?

options.A: Hydralazine
options.B: Magnesium sulphate
options.C: Diazepam
options.D: Phenytoin

explanation: Magnesium sulphate is the standard, safest drug used to stop and prevent eclamptic fits. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T6#BMP124_U3_T6_h2)

question: A patient has a lung condition that increases the thickness of their alveolar membranes. What is the direct physiological result of this change?

options.A: Complete cessation of cellular respiration
options.B: Slower diffusion of oxygen into the bloodstream
options.C: Immediate breakdown of the lipid bilayer
options.D: Faster transport of glucose into lung cells

explanation: A thicker membrane increases distance, which reduces the efficiency and speed of gas diffusion in the lungs. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T3#BMP111_U1_T3_h5)

question: Where does the lymphatic fluid from the ovaries primarily drain to?

options.A: Popliteal lymph nodes
options.B: Axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Superficial inguinal nodes
options.D: Lumbar and aortic nodes

explanation: Because ovaries originate high in the posterior abdominal wall during embryonic development, their lymphatic drainage travels up to the lumbar and aortic nodes. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T2#BMP210_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which specific laboratory value drops significantly when a patient enters the consumption phase of DIC?

options.A: Hemoglobin concentration
options.B: Serum potassium level
options.C: Fibrinogen level
options.D: White blood cell count

explanation: Fibrinogen is a key clotting protein that gets rapidly used up during the clotting phase, leading to very low levels during DIC. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of maintaining waste logbooks in a maternity unit?

options.A: To record the personal contact details of every mother
options.B: To track how many babies are born each day
options.C: To create a clear audit trail proving safe disposal and regulatory compliance
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of electricity used

explanation: Logbooks track waste volumes and disposal methods to satisfy health inspectors and environmental protection agencies. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT required when documenting vital signs in a clinical chart?

options.A: The time the assessment was performed
options.B: The personal home address of the patient
options.C: The numerical values obtained
options.D: The exact date of the measurement

explanation: While patient identification is necessary on the folder, the home address is not a required component of a vital sign entry. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T2#BMP110_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of eating by mouth compared to other feeding methods?

options.A: It guarantees maximum daily weight gain
options.B: It completely eliminates the risk of infection
options.C: It stops all digestive secretions immediately
options.D: It preserves normal gastrointestinal function

explanation: Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut working normally and maintains mucosal health better than artificial routes. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h1)

question: What is the best way for a midwife to begin explaining a growth chart to an anxious mother?

options.A: Immediately scold the mother for failing to feed the baby proper meals.
options.B: Focus entirely on the negative drops and ignore any upward trends.
options.C: Hand over the chart silently without offering any verbal explanations.
options.D: Highlight positive gains and steady progress before discussing any worries.

explanation: Starting with positive reinforcement builds trust and keeps mothers open to receiving guidance on areas that need improvement. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T3#BMP222_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is financial cost an important counseling point when a mother chooses formula feeding?

options.A: Fathers refuse to buy baby food unless midwives approve the brand
options.B: Inability to afford continuous supplies can lead to dangerous dilution or early use of unsafe substitutes
options.C: Hospitals require proof of monthly income before selling infant formula tins
options.D: Expensive formulas automatically contain higher amounts of essential vitamins

explanation: Financial strain often causes parents to dilute formula with extra water to make it last longer, severely compromising infant nutrition. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T8#BMP214_U3_T8_h7)

question: How do opposing lawyers typically use missing or messy entries during a malpractice lawsuit?

options.A: To prove the hospital has excellent administrative standards
options.B: To request a higher financial grant for the maternity unit
options.C: To argue negligence and lack of standard care by the midwife
options.D: To support the midwife's verbal testimony during cross-examination

explanation: Gaps and messy writing create doubt, allowing lawyers to convince the court that proper monitoring and interventions were neglected. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which clinical finding is a hallmark indicator of severe malaria in pregnancy?

options.A: Slight elevation in blood pressure
options.B: Impaired consciousness or prostration
options.C: Mild swelling of the lower ankles
options.D: A single episode of morning sickness

explanation: Severe malaria affects vital organ systems, leading to danger signs like confusion, extreme weakness (prostration), or coma. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T5#BMP221_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why must sexual partners of a patient treated for trichomoniasis also receive treatment?

options.A: To prevent rapid reinfection of the index patient
options.B: To boost the immune system of the male partner
options.C: To cure a co-existing urinary tract infection
options.D: To prevent permanent male sterility

explanation: Treating only one partner leaves the door open for the parasite to be passed right back during their next sexual encounter. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of worsening blood pressure issues in pregnancy?

options.A: Painful contractions of the uterus
options.B: Increased appetite for sweet foods
options.C: Frequent cramping in the calves
options.D: Persistent frontal headache

explanation: A severe, unyielding headache is a classic symptom of cerebral vessel irritability and impending complications from pregnancy hypertension. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T2#BMP221_U3_T2_h3)

question: What distinguishes postpartum psychosis from postpartum blues?

options.A: Occurrence strictly on the very first day in the delivery ward
options.B: Physical breast pain caused by engorgement
options.C: Presence of severe symptoms like hallucinations and detachment from reality
options.D: Mild sadness that disappears after a single good night of sleep

explanation: Postpartum psychosis is a severe psychiatric emergency involving lost touch with reality, unlike the mild mood swings of the blues. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T3#BMP212_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why are school-aged children generally more susceptible to contracting new infections compared to mature adults?

options.A: Their diet lacks sufficient carbohydrates for energy
options.B: Their immune systems are still developing and gaining experience
options.C: They spend more hours sleeping during the afternoon
options.D: They wear school uniforms that trap excessive heat

explanation: Children have not yet been exposed to as many pathogens as adults, meaning their bodies are still building up natural defenses. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T3#BMP126_U3_T3_h1)

question: What dangerous complication can happen if you pull on the umbilical cord without pushing the uterus upward?

options.A: Cervical laceration
options.B: Eclamptic seizure
options.C: Amniotic fluid embolism
options.D: Uterine inversion

explanation: Pulling the cord without providing counter-pressure to hold the uterus in place can pull the organ inside out. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why does high intake of preformed vitamin A carry a risk of birth defects while eating beta-carotene from vegetables does not?

options.A: Plant carotene cannot cross the placental barrier under any circumstance
options.B: Preformed vitamin A destroys all circulating hormones in the placenta
options.C: Beta-carotene is water-soluble and gets immediately excreted through sweat
options.D: The body strictly regulates the conversion of plant carotene into active vitamin A

explanation: The body only converts as much beta-carotene into vitamin A as it needs, preventing the toxic buildup seen with preformed retinol supplements. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h5)

question: A woman visits a primary health clinic for family planning advice. What should the midwife recognize about this service?

options.A: It is completely unrelated to maternal and child health outcomes
options.B: It is classified strictly as a pediatric curative intervention
options.C: It forms part of the early foundation of maternal health
options.D: It should only be offered after a woman has completed her family size

explanation: Family planning is an integral entry point into the MCH continuum, safeguarding future maternal and child wellbeing. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h3)

question: How do dermal blood vessels respond when a person is exposed to cold environmental temperatures?

options.A: They completely shut down all metabolic activity
options.B: They dilate widely to let excess heat escape rapidly
options.C: They constrict to keep warm blood closer to internal organs
options.D: They rupture to stimulate new capillary growth

explanation: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin surface in the cold, minimizing heat loss and protecting core body temperature. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T2#BMP111_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which everyday activity connects patient care directly to a maternity unit's financial costs?

options.A: Writing hospital policies for public health programs
options.B: Conducting research on rare obstetric complications
options.C: Designing architectural layouts for new delivery suites
options.D: Scheduling staff shifts and requesting consumables

explanation: Daily tasks like using supplies and organizing shift rosters directly consume the unit's financial resources. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T3#BMP312_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main reason health data is combined as it moves from local facilities up to the federal level?

options.A: To hide the names of individual patients from local government workers
options.B: To reduce the physical weight of paper documents being transported
options.C: To create summary reports that give a national overview of health trends
options.D: To ensure that rural clinics stop keeping their own local records

explanation: Aggregation combines thousands of individual entries into manageable statistics that show broad public health patterns across the country. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T1#BMP123_U5_T1_h5)

question: A fifteen-year-old visits a midwife asking about contraception but begs the midwife not to tell her mother. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Promise absolute secrecy under all possible circumstances without exception
options.B: Refuse to talk to her until her mother arrives at the clinic
options.C: Assure her of confidentiality while explaining the limits regarding safety and abuse
options.D: Threaten to report her to the school authorities immediately

explanation: Midwives must protect client privacy while being honest about mandatory reporting rules if a minor faces severe abuse or danger. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T9#BMP126_U2_T9_h5)

question: What type of germ causes measles?

options.A: A bacterium
options.B: A parasite
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A virus

explanation: Measles is caused by a virus. Because it is viral, antibiotics do not work against it. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T1#BMP222_U2_T1_h1)

question: A woman in her second trimester asks if she should start folic acid now to prevent spina bifida. What is the midwife's best response?

options.A: Insist that she stops taking all vitamins immediately because it is too late
options.B: Explain that the neural tube has already formed, but continue folic acid for overall blood health
options.C: Advise her to schedule an emergency surgical consultation
options.D: Double her daily dose to make up for the missed first trimester

explanation: While the preventive window for neural tube defects has passed by the second trimester, folic acid remains vital for preventing maternal anemia and supporting general fetal growth. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T3#BMP220_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the main job of plasmin after a blood vessel heals?

options.A: To stimulate rapid production of new platelets
options.B: To constrict smooth muscle in damaged walls
options.C: To break down and dissolve the fibrin clot
options.D: To convert prothrombin directly into thrombin

explanation: Plasmin is the enzyme that breaks down and dissolves the fibrin mesh once the tissue repair is complete. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T9#BMP111_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the main characteristic of passive artificial immunity?

options.A: It stimulates the bone marrow to produce lasting memory cells
options.B: It requires several booster doses over a period of many years
options.C: It takes at least one month before any antibodies appear
options.D: It provides immediate protection using ready-made antibodies

explanation: Passive immunity gives you ready-made antibodies right away so you do not have to wait for your body to make them. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T10#BMP111_U6_T10_h3)

question: Why is it important to treat the sexual partner as well when managing trichomoniasis?

options.A: To restore normal estrogen levels in the female partner
options.B: To prevent rapid reinfection from untreated partners
options.C: To prevent the development of permanent pelvic scarring
options.D: To eradicate bacteria causing secondary yeast infections

explanation: Partners often carry the infection without showing symptoms, so treating them prevents the woman from catching it again right away. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T6#BMP116_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why should midwives use validated screening tools during routine antenatal booking visits?

options.A: To calculate the exact date of spontaneous labor onset
options.B: To uncover hidden mood disorders that patients might otherwise hide
options.C: To diagnose infectious diseases transmitted during pregnancy
options.D: To replace the need for physical blood pressure checks completely

explanation: Screening tools help catch psychiatric conditions early because patients often conceal symptoms due to social stigma. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T2#BMP223_U3_T2_h4)

question: A pregnant woman asks her midwife for advice on how to improve her fat intake without buying expensive imported items. What is the best practical response?

options.A: Drink large cups of industrial machine oil every morning
options.B: Stop eating all forms of fat immediately to protect your heart
options.C: Add local ingredients like melon seeds (egusi) and groundnuts to meals
options.D: Rely entirely on synthetic vitamin pills bought from street vendors

explanation: Locally available oilseeds and nuts are rich, affordable sources of healthy fats and nutrients suited for maternal diets. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h5)

question: A postpartum woman in a hot, humid ward develops tiny itchy red bumps on her chest and back from trapped sweat. What is the likely condition?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Anhidrosis
options.C: Hyperhidrosis
options.D: Miliaria

explanation: Blocked sweat ducts trap perspiration in the skin layers, causing miliaria or prickly heat, common in humid environments. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T11#BMP111_U4_T11_h5)

question: What details must be included in the formal documentation of a perineal repair?

options.A: The mother's detailed family medical history and ancestry
options.B: The baby's exact Apgar score at five minutes after birth
options.C: The exact cost of the suture materials used in the theater
options.D: Type of repair, suture material, and practitioner's name

explanation: Recording the specifics of the tear, materials used, and the practitioner ensures clear communication for future clinical care. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h6)

question: What does the acronym MeSH stand for in medical literature searching?

options.A: Medical Subject Headings
options.B: Medical Systematic Hierarchy
options.C: Maternal Evidence System Hub
options.D: Midwifery Search History

explanation: MeSH is the controlled vocabulary thesaurus used by PubMed to index biomedical articles consistently. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is a major danger of taking NSAIDs during the third trimester of pregnancy?

options.A: Complete stoppage of the baby's kidney development
options.B: Sudden enlargement of the mother's thyroid gland
options.C: Premature closure of the foetal ductus arteriosus
options.D: Excessive weight gain and severe ankle swelling

explanation: Taking NSAIDs late in pregnancy can cause a key blood vessel in the baby's heart, the ductus arteriosus, to close too early. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T2#BMP124_U3_T2_h4)

question: What primary function does NANNM perform for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: Registering student nurses at the start of training
options.B: Inspecting nursing schools for curriculum approval
options.C: Defending their socio-economic welfare and working conditions
options.D: Conducting professional board examinations and licensing

explanation: NANNM operates as a trade union, focusing on workers' rights, salaries, and workplace safety rather than board examinations. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h3)

question: A patient with a history of stroke is coughing slightly and breathing fast when you arrive with lunch. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage them to lie flat in bed while eating
options.B: Feed them very small bites of soft food quickly
options.C: Mix all their food and liquids together in a cup
options.D: Delay feeding and assess their respiratory status

explanation: Rapid breathing and coughing indicate a high risk for aspiration, meaning feeding must be postponed until they stabilize. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which tube carrying urine from the kidney widens more during pregnancy?

options.A: Both ureters equally
options.B: Left ureter
options.C: Neither ureter widens
options.D: Right ureter

explanation: The right ureter widens more than the left because the uterus tilts to the right and the sigmoid colon cushions the left side. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T6#BMP212_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is happening when a pregnant woman's body unloads carbon dioxide into her lung alveoli?

options.A: Her lungs are preparing to make more oxygen
options.B: She is getting rid of waste gas from her blood
options.C: She is storing extra carbon dioxide to balance her blood pH
options.D: Carbon dioxide is turning into solid calcium

explanation: Carbon dioxide is a waste product from cellular work. It travels through the blood to the lungs so it can be breathed out. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h3)

question: In Primary Health Care, what does public participation actually mean?

options.A: Communities actively shaping and sharing responsibility for their health services
options.B: Government agencies taking full control of all village health clinics
options.C: Midwives making all health decisions without consulting village elders
options.D: Patients paying higher user fees to access maternity care services

explanation: Public participation means community members are active partners rather than passive recipients of healthcare services. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h1)

question: What condition must be confirmed before a craniotomy is considered?

options.A: Presence of multiple gestation with the first twin in breech position
options.B: Confirmation of fetal death or a condition incompatible with survival
options.C: Complete maternal exhaustion occurring in the latent phase of labor
options.D: Failure of the second dose of sublingual misoprostol induction

explanation: A destructive operation is only indicated when there is absolute certainty that the fetus cannot survive or is already dead. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T5#BMP311_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why shouldn't a ward manager rely only on a staff member's job title when deciding to delegate a task?

options.A: Junior staff members always lie about their qualifications
options.B: Hospital management discourages looking at job titles
options.C: Job titles do not guarantee practical competence in every specific clinical skill
options.D: Titles change too often in Nigerian hospitals

explanation: Actual hands-on capability can vary widely among workers holding the exact same title, so individual competency checks are always necessary. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason for giving eye ointment to a newborn right after birth?

options.A: To prevent natural dryness of the newborn conjunctiva
options.B: To prevent severe eye infections from birth canal exposure
options.C: To improve the baby's early visual focus and clarity
options.D: To flush out normal vernix caseosa from the eyelids

explanation: Prophylactic eye ointment protects the newborn's eyes from harmful bacteria picked up during vaginal delivery. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T2#BMP213_U4_T2_h1)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the primary survey ABCDE approach?

options.A: Blood pressure
options.B: Breathing
options.C: Brain function
options.D: Bleeding

explanation: In the emergency ABCDE protocol, B stands for evaluating the patient's breathing and chest movement. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T8#BMP110_U7_T8_h4)

question: How does the typical appetite of a child with marasmus compare to one with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Kwashiorkor children eat voraciously while marasmus children lose interest
options.B: Both groups of children refuse all forms of food completely
options.C: Marasmus children are usually hungry; kwashiorkor children are anoretic
options.D: Neither condition has any impact on the child's daily appetite

explanation: Children with marasmus are typically alert and hungry, whereas kwashiorkor patients suffer from severe anorexia and lack interest in food. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T2#BMP118_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of family planning in primary health care?

options.A: Treating all forms of sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Helping couples decide the spacing and timing of children
options.C: Completely stopping population growth in rural communities
options.D: Forcing families to have a maximum of two children

explanation: Family planning gives individuals and couples the information and means to choose when and how often to have children. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T1#BMP126_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why are pregnant women with acute pyelonephritis usually admitted to the hospital?

options.A: To perform immediate surgery to remove the affected kidney
options.B: To restrict all fluid intake until the infection clears
options.C: To give general anesthesia during urine collection
options.D: To prevent severe maternal infection spread and early labor using intravenous treatment

explanation: Pregnancy lowers the body's resistance, making hospital admission and IV antibiotics necessary to quickly control the infection and protect the baby. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by health workers in routine HMIS data collection?

options.A: Irregular electricity supply affecting electronic record devices
options.B: Excessive availability of high-speed internet in rural clinics
options.C: Heavy paperwork burden that takes time away from patient care
options.D: Shortages of dedicated records personnel in primary facilities

explanation: Rural primary health centers in Nigeria typically suffer from poor or absent internet connectivity rather than an excess of it. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T1#BMP123_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective strategy for preventing unsafe adolescent abortions?

options.A: Establishing confidential youth-friendly reproductive clinics
options.B: Withholding contraceptive information to discourage premarital sex
options.C: Dispelling common myths about modern birth control methods
options.D: Providing comprehensive sexuality education in local schools

explanation: Hiding contraceptive information does not stop sexual activity; it only increases the incidence of unprotected sex and unwanted pregnancies. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is a major advantage of transactional leadership in a hospital?

options.A: Complete freedom to ignore hospital shift schedules
options.B: High role clarity and consistent following of procedures
options.C: Total elimination of all administrative paperwork
options.D: Rapid creation of unverified alternative drug treatments

explanation: Transactional leadership ensures everyone knows their specific tasks and follows standard operating procedures consistently. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T7#BMP312_U1_T7_h4)

question: What solution is applied to the cervix during a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) screening?

options.A: Vinegar
options.B: Hydrogen peroxide
options.C: Iodine
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Acetic acid is essentially diluted vinegar, which causes abnormal precancerous cells on the cervix to turn white for easy spotting. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h5)

question: What directional term describes a body part located closer to the head?

options.A: Inferior
options.B: Lateral
options.C: Superior
options.D: Distal

explanation: Superior indicates a position higher up or closer to the head. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T1#BMP111_U1_T1_h3)

question: What effect do phytates and oxalates have on dietary magnesium?

options.A: They transform magnesium into a vitamin
options.B: They speed up digestion so magnesium is absorbed faster
options.C: They dissolve the intestinal lining to let minerals pass freely
options.D: They bind to magnesium in the gut and reduce its absorption

explanation: Phytates and oxalates attach to minerals in the digestive tract, lowering how much magnesium enters the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T8#BMP118_U2_T8_h4)

question: In Graves' disease, the body produces autoantibodies that attach to which specific receptors on the thyroid cells?

options.A: Estrogen receptors
options.B: Thyrotropin receptors
options.C: Insulin receptors
options.D: Adrenergic receptors

explanation: Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins target the TSH (thyrotropin) receptors, continuously tricking the gland into releasing more hormones. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T5#BMP216_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following describes the main function of a bed cradle?

options.A: To provide a soft cushion directly under the patient's lower back
options.B: To anchor the patient firmly so they do not slide down
options.C: To elevate the patient's head for easier feeding
options.D: To keep the weight of top bedclothes off the patient's body

explanation: Cradles act as a physical bridge over the patient, stopping heavy blankets from pressing painfully against sensitive skin or limbs. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h2)

question: How does the mental state of a child with marasmus usually differ from a child with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Marasmic infants show no emotion while others laugh
options.B: Marasmic infants are alert and irritable, whereas kwashiorkor children are apathetic
options.C: Both conditions cause the exact same extreme lethargy
options.D: Marasmic infants are in a coma while others are hyperactive

explanation: Children with marasmus stay mentally alert and often fret, whereas kwashiorkor causes marked apathy and lethargy. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why has occupational health expanded beyond traditional machine safety?

options.A: Hospitals no longer treat physical injuries related to heavy tools
options.B: Modern perspectives now embrace total worker health including mental and social factors
options.C: Machinery is no longer considered dangerous in modern industrial settings
options.D: Factory owners requested reduced oversight on equipment maintenance

explanation: Our understanding has grown to include mental health and social well-being alongside physical safety. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T1#BMP126_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why should educators avoid trick questions or confusing wording in midwifery exams?

options.A: They make the grading guide too hard to calculate
options.B: They test reading confusion instead of actual clinical knowledge
options.C: They stop students from finishing the exam within one hour
options.D: They take too long to type on a standard computer

explanation: Trick questions measure a student's ability to decipher confusing English rather than their understanding of midwifery. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T9#BMP312_U3_T9_h5)

question: Where are fetal heart sounds typically auscultated when the baby is in an OP position?

options.A: High up near the top of the fundus
options.B: Far out toward the mother's flank
options.C: Directly in the center of the umbilicus
options.D: Directly over the mother's pubic bone

explanation: Because the baby's chest and back are turned toward the mother's back, the heart sounds travel outward and are best heard far to the side. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way to support a mother whose baby is under phototherapy?

options.A: Allowing short breaks for bonding when the lights are switched off
options.B: Explaining why the baby must wear tiny patches over their eyes
options.C: Telling her to stop visiting until the phototherapy is completely finished
options.D: Encouraging her to express breast milk for regular feeding times

explanation: Separating the mother from her baby harms bonding and lactation; mothers should be included in care whenever possible. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T7#BMP220_U1_T7_h4)

question: Where is the safest place to collect a urine sample from a patient who has an indwelling urinary catheter?

options.A: The open end of the drainage bag outlet
options.B: The bottom drainage bag tap
options.C: The junction connecting the tubing to the bag
options.D: The specialized needleless sampling port

explanation: The sampling port lets midwives collect fresh urine while keeping the system closed and protected from outside germs. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T6#BMP110_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following describes the correct approach to airway clearance for a vigorous newborn?

options.A: Routine deep suctioning of the mouth and nose
options.B: Immediate mechanical suctioning of the trachea
options.C: Washing the upper airway with sterile water
options.D: No routine suctioning if the baby is crying well

explanation: Healthy, vigorous babies clear their own airways naturally and do not need routine bulb suctioning. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T3#BMP212_U3_T3_h2)

question: When a midwife measures the diagonal conjugate during an examination, what is she trying to estimate indirectly?

options.A: The outlet anteroposterior diameter
options.B: The bisischial diameter
options.C: The transverse inlet diameter
options.D: The obstetric conjugate

explanation: The diagonal conjugate is measured with fingers to estimate the true obstetric conjugate, which cannot be reached directly. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T2#BMP210_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why use standardized subject headings instead of only free-text keywords?

options.A: It captures relevant articles even if authors use different synonyms for the same concept
options.B: It prevents the database from crashing during heavy internet traffic
options.C: It guarantees that every paper found is completely free to read
options.D: It automatically translates every article into the local language

explanation: Subject headings group different word variations under one standard term so important studies are not missed due to naming differences. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary role of the artemisinin component in an ACT regimen?

options.A: To provide long-term protection against reinfection
options.B: To clear the bulk of parasites rapidly
options.C: To prevent secondary bacterial infections
options.D: To soothe gastrointestinal upset in the patient

explanation: Artemisinin derivatives act very fast to reduce the parasite load in the patient's blood during the first few days of illness. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T12#BMP124_U4_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an exchange transfusion in a newborn?

options.A: To remove toxic bilirubin and damaged red blood cells quickly
options.B: To provide extra iron for long-term storage in the liver
options.C: To permanently cure all congenital heart defects
options.D: To increase the baby's birth weight within twenty-four hours

explanation: An exchange transfusion physically extracts high levels of bilirubin and destroying cells, replacing them with healthy donor blood. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T7#BMP220_U1_T7_h5)

question: What early pregnancy condition is a major cause of severe dehydration and mineral loss?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Physiological hemodilution
options.C: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Hyperemesis gravidarum involves severe, ongoing vomiting that quickly drains essential body fluids and minerals. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h6)

question: How does the FEFO principle guide daily stock management in a midwifery clinic?

options.A: Newer shipments are always used before older inventory
options.B: Freezer-safe vials are kept separate from heat-sensitive ones
options.C: Vaccines expiring sooner are used before those expiring later
options.D: Vaccines brought back from outreach are discarded first

explanation: FEFO (First Expire, First Out) prevents valuable medicine from spoiling on the shelf past its expiration date. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason midwives give eye care to a newborn right after birth?

options.A: To test if the baby has normal eye movement
options.B: To improve how clearly the baby can see at birth
options.C: To stop the eyelids from sticking together from sleep
options.D: To prevent severe eye infections from birth canal bacteria

explanation: Eye prophylaxis protects the newborn's eyes from harmful germs picked up during delivery. [learn more](BMP214_U2_T4#BMP214_U2_T4_h1)

question: How should a midwife handle a pregnant client complaining of mild nausea from her antiretroviral drugs?

options.A: Advise the woman to stop taking all drugs until the nausea completely stops
options.B: Switch her immediately to second-line injectable medications without consultation
options.C: Offer practical management tips like taking drugs with food and encourage continuation
options.D: Tell her that nausea means the drugs are not working in her body

explanation: Midwives should support clients through minor side effects with practical advice rather than encouraging dangerous treatment interruptions. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T6#BMP213_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important to get zinc in your diet every single day?

options.A: Zinc is rapidly destroyed by stomach acid every day
options.B: The kidneys filter out all stored zinc within hours
options.C: The body lacks a dedicated storage depot for zinc
options.D: Micro minerals cannot bind to proteins for storage

explanation: Because the human body does not maintain a specialized storage organ for zinc, it depends on a continuous daily supply from food. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which type of amino acids must come from food because the body cannot make them?

options.A: Saturated amino acids
options.B: Simple amino acids
options.C: Non-essential amino acids
options.D: Essential amino acids

explanation: Essential amino acids cannot be made by the human body and must be supplied through diet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h2)

question: At what developmental stage do parents usually first notice skeletal deformities like bowlegs in rickets?

options.A: Only after the permanent teeth have erupted
options.B: During the first month of exclusive breastfeeding
options.C: Immediately at birth before feeding begins
options.D: When the child starts standing and walking

explanation: The physical stress of gravity and weight-bearing forces soft, unmineralized leg bones to bow outward. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T20#BMP111_U2_T20_h4)

question: Why is it important for a midwife to validate a client's concerns about neighborhood stories?

options.A: It helps the client feel heard without being judged or dismissed
options.B: It allows the midwife to avoid giving actual clinical advice
options.C: It proves that neighborhood gossip is always medically accurate
options.D: It ensures the client purchases expensive branded supplements

explanation: Validating fears builds rapport and shows respect, making the client much more receptive to accurate health information. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T4#BMP224_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Convulsions or abnormal shaking
options.B: Passing regular yellow-brown stools
options.C: Inability to suck or feed at all
options.D: Chest indrawing when breathing

explanation: Yellow-brown stools are normal for a feeding newborn, whereas poor feeding, seizures, and respiratory distress are serious danger signs. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which Excel function calculates the arithmetic average of a column of numbers?

options.A: =COUNT()
options.B: =TOTAL()
options.C: =MIDPOINT()
options.D: =AVERAGE()

explanation: The =AVERAGE formula in Excel automatically adds up a range of cells and divides by the total count of numbers in that range. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T5#BMP225_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why does a baby's head make automatic twisting and turning movements as it travels down the birth canal?

options.A: Uterine contractions push the fetus down against resistance from the pelvic floor.
options.B: The mother actively pushes the baby in different directions using her abdominal muscles.
options.C: Midwives manually rotate the baby's head during routine vaginal examinations.
options.D: The fetus deliberately adjusts its body to find a more comfortable position.

explanation: As the uterus contracts and pushes the baby downward, the sloping bones and muscles of the pelvis act like a slide, forcing the head to passively turn and find the easiest path. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T4#BMP212_U2_T4_h1)

question: What describes the concept of self-actualization in patient care?

options.A: Maintaining stable blood pressure and normal body temperature
options.B: Complying strictly with a hospital medication timetable
options.C: Attaining financial security after paying hospital bills
options.D: Reaching one's full potential and finding personal meaning

explanation: Self-actualization represents the highest level of personal growth, fulfillment, and realization of one's capabilities. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in a rural maternity center?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal booking registers
options.B: To audit the financial expenses of the maternity clinic
options.C: To calculate the monthly salaries of community health workers
options.D: To act as an early warning system against maternal and neonatal infections

explanation: Surveillance tracks health data continuously so facilities can spot unusual illness patterns early before they spread widely. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h1)

question: How should a community midwife handle a local cultural practice that poses a clear health risk to a pregnant woman?

options.A: Call the police immediately to arrest everyone involved in the traditional custom
options.B: Publicly insult village elders who support the practice during community meetings
options.C: Ignore the practice completely and allow the woman to face any resulting complications
options.D: Use respectful dialogue and health education to guide the family toward safe alternatives

explanation: Respectful communication and patient education work best to change dangerous traditions without alienating the community. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T1#BMP215_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of appropriate technology in primary health care?

options.A: To introduce high-tech computers into every rural clinic
options.B: To replace all traditional practices with imported Western machinery
options.C: To lower the cost of healthcare by eliminating trained staff
options.D: To provide solutions that fit local economic and environmental realities

explanation: Appropriate technology focuses on tools and methods that match what a local community can afford, maintain, and safely use. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T7#BMP117_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following practices should a midwife NOT recommend for a pregnant woman with leg varicosities?

options.A: Standing in one spot for long hours without a break
options.B: Elevating the legs above hip level during rest
options.C: Walking regularly at a moderate and comfortable pace
options.D: Sleeping on the left side to ease pelvic pressure

explanation: Prolonged static standing increases blood pooling and worsens discomfort, so it should be avoided. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T14#BMP212_U1_T14_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT an acceptable way to handle patient records?

options.A: Leaving physical case notes open on a public desk for visitors to see
options.B: Keeping computer screens turned away from public view at the nursing station
options.C: Limiting chart access strictly to the healthcare team directly involved
options.D: Storing active patient files inside a securely locked ward cabinet

explanation: Leaving sensitive case files exposed to the public violates patient confidentiality and privacy rights. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h4)

question: What name is given to hyphae that lack cross-walls and have a continuous cytoplasm with multiple nuclei?

options.A: Septate
options.B: Conidiophores
options.C: Coenocytic
options.D: Pseudohyphae

explanation: Coenocytic hyphae lack internal cross-walls, allowing free movement of cytoplasm and cell parts throughout the filament. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T1#BMP116_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is the postpartum period considered especially risky for women with this mood condition?

options.A: Physical exhaustion permanently cures underlying neurotransmitter imbalances
options.B: Breastfeeding completely blocks the absorption of all psychiatric drugs
options.C: New mothers automatically develop permanent tolerance to mood stabilizers
options.D: Hormonal crashes and sleep deprivation trigger severe mood relapses

explanation: Sudden hormonal changes and severe lack of sleep after birth are major physical triggers for a new episode. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T2#BMP223_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is explaining each step of a vaginal exam out loud to the patient so important?

options.A: It legally protects the hospital from all future lawsuits
options.B: It helps reduce anxiety and builds trust between the midwife and the woman
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which the cervix opens up
options.D: It ensures that medical students outside the room can take notes

explanation: Talking the patient through the procedure removes the fear of the unknown and gives her a sense of control. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h6)

question: A woman visits the clinic three months after delivery following a pregnancy with pre-eclampsia. What advice should the midwife prioritize?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent her kidneys from working too hard
options.B: Take high-dose iron supplements daily to prevent stroke
options.C: Schedule regular blood pressure checks and adopt heart-healthy lifestyle habits
options.D: Avoid any future pregnancies entirely because the risk is always one hundred percent

explanation: Because of increased cardiovascular risks, ongoing blood pressure checks and healthy habits like balanced diet and exercise are essential for long-term health. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T7#BMP221_U3_T7_h4)

question: A new mother is worried that a certain contraceptive will cause heavy bleeding and make her husband unhappy. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Delay all contraception counseling until her husband can attend the clinic
options.B: Tell her that cultural beliefs about bleeding are completely outdated
options.C: Listen actively to her concerns and discuss side effect management options
options.D: Insist that she choose an intrauterine device because it has no hormones

explanation: Listening to a client's personal and marital worries builds trust and helps her find a method she feels comfortable using. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of loosening a tourniquet after it has been tightened for a while?

options.A: It stops the heart from beating completely
options.B: It permanently stains the skin a dark purple color
options.C: It always causes the limb to heal crookedly
options.D: It can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure and release built-up toxins

explanation: Releasing trapped metabolic waste and sudden blood loss return into circulation can shock the cardiovascular system. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T3#BMP110_U7_T3_h4)

question: Which finding is typical for a newborn with moderate hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (Stage 2)?

options.A: Deep coma with completely absent vital signs
options.B: Normal alertness with no abnormal reflexes at all
options.C: Lethargy, low muscle tone, and a weak suck reflex
options.D: Extreme rigid muscle tone and constant crying

explanation: Stage 2 moderate HIE presents with decreased activity, low muscle tone, and poor feeding responses alongside possible seizure activity. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T4#BMP220_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do midwives check the bones and muscles during antenatal visits?

options.A: To measure the exact weight gained during the pregnancy
options.B: To evaluate the internal maturation of the developing fetus
options.C: To diagnose underlying congenital heart defects in the mother
options.D: To distinguish normal pregnancy changes from orthopedic problems

explanation: Midwives perform these assessments mainly to separate expected pregnancy discomforts from actual bone or muscle issues. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following practices is NOT a helpful community-level strategy for preventing obstructed labor?

options.A: Improving transport availability for rural obstetric emergencies
options.B: Educating families to recognize danger signs quickly
options.C: Promoting early booking and regular antenatal attendance
options.D: Encouraging home births managed by untrained attendants

explanation: Untrained birth attendants cannot manage mechanical complications, making home births without skilled care a major risk factor for delayed referrals and obstruction. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T3#BMP311_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is another common name for parasympatholytic drugs?

options.A: Cholinergic agonists
options.B: Sympathomimetics
options.C: Anticholinergics
options.D: Beta-blockers

explanation: Parasympatholytics block acetylcholine and are widely known as anticholinergic agents because they oppose the effects of the parasympathetic nervous system. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T5#BMP124_U2_T5_h1)

question: A newborn baby shows signs of respiratory distress and sepsis shortly after a vaginal delivery. Which maternal bacterium is the most likely cause?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Group B Streptococcus

explanation: Early-onset neonatal sepsis appearing shortly after birth is most commonly linked to vertical transmission of GBS from a colonized birth canal. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T4#BMP116_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why do midwives prefer a daily symptom diary over asking a patient to remember past cycles?

options.A: Patients often struggle to accurately recall past symptoms from memory
options.B: Hospital insurance policies strictly forbid verbal health histories
options.C: Daily diaries instantly cure the underlying hormonal imbalance
options.D: Memory recall is always completely accurate without any flaws

explanation: Memory can be biased by current feelings, making prospective daily tracking essential to prove the symptoms are truly cyclical. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T5#BMP310_U3_T5_h4)

question: What level of processing is required for medical equipment that enters sterile body tissues or the vascular system?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Ultraviolet sun drying
options.D: Simple soap washing

explanation: Critical items touching sterile tissues must be completely free of all microbial life, which requires proper sterilization. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T6#BMP220_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why might a doctor order blood tests for a patient with severe, returning mouth ulcers?

options.A: To prove the infection is bacterial
options.B: To check when the patient last brushed their teeth
options.C: To measure how much saliva the glands produce
options.D: To check for underlying issues like vitamin deficiencies or anemia

explanation: Returning or lasting stomatitis can be a sign of internal health issues, such as low iron, folate, or vitamin B12. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T2#BMP125_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT part of standard midwifery care for a postpartum woman recovering from a strep infection?

options.A: Assessing the lochia for colour, amount, and odour
options.B: Administering prescribed antibiotic therapy on schedule
options.C: Monitoring maternal temperature and pulse regularly
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent overhydration

explanation: Infected postpartum women need adequate hydration to support recovery and manage fever, not fluid restriction. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T4#BMP116_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is a common clinical feature of an intestinal tapeworm?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the whites of the eyes
options.B: High spiking fevers with severe skin rashes
options.C: Vague abdominal discomfort and weight loss
options.D: Sudden paralysis of the lower extremities

explanation: Tapeworms often cause mild gastrointestinal complaints like abdominal pain, nausea, and weight loss despite a normal appetite. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T8#BMP116_U3_T8_h4)

question: What indicates that a septic abortion has progressed from Stage 1 to Stage 2?

options.A: The fetus has been delivered completely alive and healthy
options.B: The patient's blood pressure has returned completely to normal
options.C: The bleeding has stopped without any medical intervention
options.D: The infection has spread beyond the uterus into pelvic tissues

explanation: Stage 2 represents the extension of the infection outside the uterine walls into the surrounding pelvic structures and peritoneum. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h3)

question: By approximately what percentage does maternal blood volume increase during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Up to 70 percent
options.B: Up to 10 percent
options.C: Up to 40 percent
options.D: Up to 90 percent

explanation: Maternal blood volume expands significantly during pregnancy to meet the demands of the fetus and placenta, reaching about a 40 percent increase near term. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T1#BMP125_U2_T1_h1)

question: When is the best time for a midwife to count the fetal heart rate during active labor?

options.A: Strictly while a contraction is peaking
options.B: Immediately after a contraction ends
options.C: Right before the membranes rupture
options.D: Only when the mother pushes to deliver

explanation: Counting right after a contraction helps the midwife identify late decelerations and recovery patterns safely. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of using a spacer with a Metered-Dose Inhaler?

options.A: It turns liquid medications into intravenous solutions automatically
options.B: It overcomes poor hand-breath coordination by holding the spray in a chamber
options.C: It speeds up the heart rate so the drug absorbs faster
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any prescription from a doctor

explanation: Spacers capture the medication cloud so patients do not have to press the canister and breathe in at the exact same millisecond. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T10#BMP125_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the normal resting range for a baby's heart rate?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 120 beats per minute
options.C: 140 to 180 beats per minute
options.D: 110 to 160 beats per minute

explanation: A healthy resting baby's heart rate normally falls between 110 and 160 beats per minute. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h7)

question: When is the best time for midwives to start talking about family planning with pregnant women?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: When the child is weaned from the breast
options.C: Only at the six-week postnatal check
options.D: During routine antenatal care visits

explanation: Bringing up family planning early during antenatal visits gives couples plenty of time to discuss and choose their postpartum options before the baby arrives. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h3)

question: A patient continues to bleed heavily despite trying bimanual compression, medications, a balloon, and a B-Lynch suture. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Perform manual removal of the placenta a second time
options.B: Remove all intravenous lines and transfer the patient home
options.C: Proceed immediately to emergency obstetric hysterectomy
options.D: Wait another two hours to see if oxytocin starts working

explanation: When all conservative measures fail to stop the bleeding, prompt removal of the uterus prevents fatal shock. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which term describes an inversion where the fundus has turned inside out but remains above the internal os?

options.A: Total prolapse
options.B: Third-degree inversion
options.C: Incomplete inversion
options.D: Complete inversion

explanation: An incomplete inversion means the fundus has collapsed inward, but it has not descended past the cervical os. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T2#BMP311_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is hair clipping preferred over traditional razor shaving for pre-operative skin preparation?

options.A: Razors are too expensive to purchase in most government hospitals
options.B: Hair clipping takes less time for busy nursing staff to complete
options.C: Clipping completely stops hair from ever growing back on the abdomen
options.D: Razor shaving causes micro-abrasions that increase infection risks

explanation: Tiny cuts from razors create entry points for bacteria, making surgical site infections more likely compared to clean clipping. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T2#BMP120_U4_T2_h4)

question: What drop factor is typically associated with a standard microdrip infusion set?

options.A: 60 drops per milliliter
options.B: 10 drops per milliliter
options.C: 20 drops per milliliter
options.D: 15 drops per milliliter

explanation: Microdrip sets deliver 60 drops per milliliter, making it easy to calculate drops per minute as equal to milliliters per hour. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T6#BMP120_U2_T6_h6)

question: Who was the first person to see tiny moving organisms using simple handmade microscopes?

options.A: Robert Koch
options.B: Ignaz Semmelweis
options.C: Louis Pasteur
options.D: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek

question: Why is hourly urine output measurement critical for a patient receiving care for severe preeclampsia?

question: What is the main difference between an emergency and an elective caesarean section?

question: Which of the following assessments is NOT required before increasing an oxytocin infusion rate?

question: Which pathogen is the leading cause of severe, dehydrating watery diarrhea in infants worldwide?

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing responsibility when caring for a hospitalized pregnant malaria patient?

question: How should a midwife approach teaching reproductive health to teenagers in a school environment?

question: Why is community sensitization by midwives considered critical alongside legal prohibitions?

question: Why might a complete blood count be ordered for a patient with a suspected GI problem?

question: How long does morning joint stiffness typically last in osteoarthritis?

question: What is one main objective of maternal and child health programs in primary health care?

question: Why do COCs help decrease the risk of iron-deficiency anemia in many regular users?

explanation: Many women opt for supported home births to stay close to their families and avoid the financial and logistical challenges of reaching distant hospitals. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T1#BMP215_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for supporting a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: No single profession can meet the complex medical, legal, and social needs of the survivor
options.B: Social workers handle all clinical diagnoses of physical trauma
options.C: Midwives are legally prohibited from speaking with victims of violence alone
options.D: Hospital administrative rules require at least five staff members per patient

explanation: Recovery requires medical care, psychological support, social services, and legal protection, which only a coordinated team can provide. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h7)

question: Trauma often disrupts which key element required for healthy mother-infant bonding?

options.A: Strict feeding schedules
options.B: High household income
options.C: Emotional availability
options.D: Extended family housing

explanation: Bonding relies on a mother being emotionally available to notice and respond to her baby, which trauma can make very difficult. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T4#BMP223_U2_T4_h5)

question: An alarm goes off showing a very low heart rate on the monitor. What is the first thing the midwife should do?

options.A: Check the physical status of the baby directly
options.B: Silence the alarm and wait for five minutes
options.C: Turn off the monitor sound permanently
options.D: Disconnect all the sensor leads immediately

explanation: Loose cords or machine errors can cause false alarms, so the midwife must always check the baby's actual condition first. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T1#BMP220_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which ion rushes INTO the neuron when an action potential starts?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Chloride
options.C: Potassium
options.D: Sodium

explanation: When a neuron is stimulated, sodium channels open and sodium ions flood inward, changing the electrical charge across the membrane. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is NOT a feature of standard T-cell activation and response?

options.A: Requirement for antigens to be presented on MHC molecules
options.B: Induction of apoptosis in targeted rogue cells
options.C: Direct interaction with infected or abnormal host cells
options.D: Secretion of free-floating antibodies into blood plasma

explanation: Antibody secretion is the job of B-cells and plasma cells in humoral immunity, not T-cells. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T6#BMP111_U6_T6_h5)

question: What condition involving intrauterine scar tissue can result from aggressive uterine curettage?

options.A: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Asherman's syndrome
options.D: Cervical incompetence

explanation: Scraping the uterine cavity too aggressively destroys the lining, causing walls to stick together, which is known as Asherman's syndrome. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h5)
